w: Opened November 2025 after two decades of construction, two kilometres from the pyramids. Houses over 100,000 artefacts including the complete Tutankhamun collection displayed together for the first time, plus a grand staircase lined with colossal statues climbing toward panoramic pyramid views.
why: Opened Nov 2025; largest archaeological museum devoted to one civilisation, finally showing the full Tutankhamun trove together.

w: Opened May 2025 inside a restored 1923 Holland-America Line warehouse on the Katendrecht docks, the world's first museum devoted entirely to migration. Its centrepiece Tornado stair, a swirling double-helix of polished steel, rises through a suspended cloud of 2,000 donated suitcases.
s: First museum of migration, in an old dock shed
why: Opened May 2025; MAD Architects' warehouse conversion is the first museum anywhere dedicated solely to migration.

area: Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park, Hackney Wick
w: Opened May 2025 in the former 2012 Olympic media centre at Here East, giving open public access to over 250,000 objects from the V&A's working stores. Frank Lloyd Wright's dismantled 1930s office, samurai armour and stage sets sit on rolling racks visitors can walk right up to.
s: The V&A's working store, thrown open
why: Opened May 2025; a new model of museum storage-as-exhibit, letting visitors browse the V&A's reserve collection directly.

w: Opened May 2025 on a hillside above Honmura port, Tadao Ando's tenth building for Benesse Art Site Naoshima. Raw-concrete galleries sunk partly underground show contemporary art from across Asia, including new commissions by Cai Guo-Qiang, Chim Pom and Aida Makoto.
why: Opened May 2025; extends the Naoshima art-island pilgrimage with Ando's newest building, focused on Asian contemporary art.

w: Reopened October 2025 in a Haussmannian building opposite the Louvre, gutted and rebuilt by Jean Nouvel around five vertically adjustable steel platforms that let 6,500 square metres of galleries be reconfigured for every show. The opening Exposition Generale draws on four decades of the foundation's collection.
s: Cartier's art foundation, rebuilt by Nouvel
why: Reopened Oct 2025 opposite the Louvre in a radically re-engineered Jean Nouvel building with movable floor-platforms.

w: Opened September 2025 at the corner of Al-Farabi and Nazarbayev avenues, Central Asia's first private museum of modern and contemporary art. Chapman Taylor's stone-and-aluminium volumes hold over 700 works by Kazakh and Central Asian artists alongside international names.
s: Central Asia's first private art museum
why: Opened Sept 2025; largest contemporary-art institution in Central Asia, a first for a region with almost no private-museum culture.

w: Opened December 2025 in a former steel warehouse off Sukhumvit, Thailand's first international contemporary-art museum after three decades in the making. Eleven halls hold over 1,000 works from the Osathanugrah family's collection, arranged around a 1,400-square-metre courtyard.
why: Opened Dec 2025; a three-decades-anticipated private museum finally gives Bangkok a dedicated international contemporary-art home.

w: Opened December 2025 on Saadiyat Island, the UAE's national museum designed by Norman Foster with five steel wings shaped like falcon feathers that double as solar chimneys. Six galleries trace 300,000 years of Emirati history, from Bronze Age trade routes to the 1971 founding of the union.
why: Opened Dec 2025 after nearly two decades of delay; Foster + Partners' centrepiece of the Saadiyat Cultural District.

w: Opened November 2025 on Saadiyat Island, Mecanoo's geology-inspired building anchors the region's largest natural-history collection. Stan, one of the most complete Tyrannosaurus rex skeletons ever found, greets visitors in a 35,000-square-metre museum spanning 4.6 billion years of planetary history.
why: Opened Nov 2025 with the T. rex Stan as centrepiece; largest natural-history museum in the Gulf.

w: Opened April 2025 on Saadiyat Island, a 17,000-square-metre venue where teamLab's installations respond in real time to air, water and light instead of looping on a screen. Visitors wade through a fog-filled valley and a floating flower field that keep reshaping themselves through the day.
s: Immersive art that reacts to real weather
why: Opened April 2025; teamLab's first standalone Middle East venue, built around genuinely responsive rather than pre-rendered installations.

w: Reopened November 2025 in its first purpose-built home on West 125th Street after a seven-year closure. Adjaye Associates' seven-storey, 82,000-square-foot building, funded by a $300 million campaign, doubles the space of the institution devoted to artists of African descent.
s: First purpose-built home for Black art
why: Reopened Nov 2025 after 7 years closed; its first-ever purpose-built building, doubling exhibition space.

w: Opened March 2026 on Bowery at Prince Street, a seven-storey OMA-designed tower by Rem Koolhaas and Shohei Shigematsu that doubles the New Museum's exhibition space to over 20,000 square feet. The addition stands beside the original 2007 SANAA building, its metal-mesh facade answering that stack of boxes.
s: OMA's tower doubles the New Museum
why: Opened March 2026; a rare case of one starchitect building the addition to another's landmark within two decades.

w: Opened June 2026 inside Frank Gehry's Grand LA development, billed as the world's first museum of AI art. Refik Anadol's 25,000-square-foot space turns rainforest field recordings and ecological data into shifting, self-generating light installations across a Google-backed omni-sensory environment.
why: Opened June 2026; first dedicated museum for AI-generated art, from the artist behind MoMA and Sphere data-sculptures.

w: Opened April 2025 on the second floor of Crown Center, the world's first museum devoted entirely to barbecue. Themed rooms walk through wood smoke, regional sauce styles and pit culture across the American South and Midwest, ending in a shop stacked with rubs and house sauces.
why: Opened April 2025; a genuinely novel single-subject museum, the first anywhere built solely around barbecue culture.

w: Opened September 2025 as a 26,000-square-foot immersive venue outside Chicago, built by Montreal's PHI Studio with the Village of Rosemont. Launch expeditions Horizon of Khufu and Life Chronicles use motion, scent and VR to walk visitors through ancient Egypt and 4 billion years of evolution.
s: Immersive VR journeys through deep time
why: Opened Sept 2025; the Midwest's largest dedicated immersive-experience venue, from the studio behind Excurio's touring shows.

w: Opened September 2025 on the 53rd floor of Varso Tower, the European Union's tallest building at 310 metres. A 230-metre-high glass gallery wraps a full 360 degrees, putting the Palace of Culture and Science and the whole Warsaw skyline underfoot from an EU-record height.
why: Opened Sept 2025; highest public viewpoint in the European Union, atop the newly completed Varso Tower.

w: Opened March 2025 behind Lina Bo Bardi's iconic 1968 glass-and-concrete MASP, a fourteen-storey black monolith by Metro Arquitetos that nearly doubles the museum's exhibition area to almost 22,000 square metres. Underground galleries link the two buildings beneath Paulista Avenue's public plaza.
why: Opened March 2025; first major expansion of Sao Paulo's flagship art museum since its landmark 1968 building.

w: Reopened May 2023 on the Karakoy waterfront in a purpose-built Renzo Piano structure, Turkey's first museum of modern and contemporary art returning to its original harbourside site. Aluminium panels mimic the shifting light of the Bosphorus across three stacked volumes holding the permanent collection.
why: Reopened May 2023 in an all-new Renzo Piano building on its original Bosphorus-front site after years displaced.

w: Opened April 2026 inside a Zaha Hadid-designed building at the KAPSARC research campus, Saudi Arabia's first museum built around oil's cultural rather than industrial legacy. Four floors and over 350 artworks by 170 artists from 30-plus countries trace how petroleum reshaped modern life and landscape.
s: Oil's cultural history, in a Zaha Hadid shell
why: Opened April 2026; Saudi Arabia's first museum framing oil as a cultural subject rather than an industrial showcase, entry free.

w: Opened February 2025 above a live excavation site in Gujarat, India's first fully experiential archaeology museum. More than 5,000 artefacts from seven continuous occupation layers spanning 2,500 years, including Buddhist monastery remains and Indo-Greek coins, are shown beside the dig itself.
why: Opened Feb 2025; first Indian museum built directly over an active excavation, showing 2,500 years of continuous habitation.

w: Opened June 2026 inside Yeouido's landmark 63 Building, the Centre Pompidou's first Asian outpost under a Hanwha partnership. Jean-Michel Wilmotte's translucent 'box of light' fit-out houses loans from the Paris collection, opening with a Cubism survey drawing on Picasso, Braque and Leger.
why: Opened June 2026; Centre Pompidou's first branch in Asia, inside one of Seoul's most recognisable towers.

w: Opened April 2026 on Haikou's west coast, Ma Yansong's spiralling, cloud-white volume appears to float above a public plaza. Inside, a planetarium and giant-screen theatre sit alongside exhibits on tropical ecology and space science, anchoring Hainan's push to become a free-trade science hub.
why: Opened April 2026; MAD Architects' spiralling landmark, the centrepiece of Hainan's new science-education push.

w: Opened September 2025 in the Red House on Calle Aguayo, a few blocks from the better-known Blue House, this is where Frida Kahlo was actually born and later died. Run by her own descendants, it focuses on her childhood and family life rather than her marriage to Diego Rivera, with previously unseen letters and objects.
s: The house where Frida Kahlo was born
why: Opened Sept 2025; a new Kahlo museum in her actual birth-and-death house, run by descendants, distinct from the famous Casa Azul.

w: Opened December 2025 on Hamer Hall's upper terrace above the Yarra, Australia's first museum dedicated to performing-arts history. Debut show DIVA draws on the nation's largest performing-arts archive of over 850,000 objects, tracing divas from Dame Nellie Melba to Kylie Minogue.
why: Opened Dec 2025; first Australian museum dedicated to performing arts, drawing on an 850,000-object national collection.

w: Opened December 2025 in Kigali's Kimihurura district, Rwanda's first non-profit institution built solely for contemporary art. Amin Gafaranga's 777-square-metre building holds galleries, a library and artist studios, opening with Inuma: A Bird Shall Carry the Voice, a survey of Rwandan and Pan-African practice.
why: Opened Dec 2025; Rwanda's first purpose-built, non-profit contemporary-art institution, designed by a Rwandan architect.
